subject: Tenantized fleet sizing survey — Lagoon Labs pre-sales thread
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@lagoon.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenantized fleet sizing survey — initial ask

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To make our Dedicated sizing proposal tight and avoid over-commitment, could you take a pass at the short traffic snapshot below and return the CSV attached (lagoon_traffic_snapshot.csv) with a sample day and a worst-day? The key inputs we need:

- Average qps by endpoint (chat/generate/embed/rerank) by hour of day
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and expected model response length (tokens) by endpoint
- Estimated concurrent sessions and session duration distribution (p50/p90)
- Percent of calls requiring cross-session KV cache warm (stateful sessions) vs stateless requests
- Target p95 latency SLO for each endpoint and acceptable cold-start window

Quick notes: our baseline configuration assumes 1x A100-equivalent per 350 sustained chat QPS at 8k context for a mixed prompt/response of 150/250 tokens with 10% session affinity. If your workload skews towards longer contexts or heavy embedding, that materially shifts the GPU mix.

Attached: redwood_preflight_checklist.pdf — short checklist of telemetry/traffic exports that speed up sizing (timestamps, example payloads, and a prompt mix sample).

Can you return the CSV plus any sample logs (anonymized) by Friday so we can run a stress projection and put together a reserved capacity recommendation? I’ll loop in Marissa for cost modelling and Karthik for routing/affinity rules.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0122

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@lagoon.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lagoon.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Tenantized fleet sizing survey — Lagoon sample day attached

Marcus,

Thanks — attaching the CSV with a representative weekday and our Black-Friday-like peak day. Notes inline:

- Endpoints: chat (65%), embeddings (20%), generate-batch (10%), rerank (5%)
- Typical prompt/response: chat ~120 prompt / 300 response tokens; embeddings 128 tokens; generate-batch varies (avg 600 tokens)
- Concurrent sessions: baseline 420 active sessions, peak 1,900 (short spikes ~10–12 minutes avg)
- Session affinity: ~22% of sessions are stateful (user conversations that reuse KV cache across requests)
- Latency target: p95 <= 350ms for chat on our US customers; embedding p95 <= 200ms

We also included a sanitized request trace folder (drive link in the CSV) and a short note on burst traffic cadence — most bursts are east-coast morning and global launches (once per month).

Attachments: lagoon_traffic_snapshot.csv

—Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Engineering | Lagoon Labs
aisha.k@lagoon.ai | +1 (617) 555-7788
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:56:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenantized fleet sizing survey — Lagoon sample day attached

Looping in a few quick numbers so we can run options in the morning:

- With Aisha's numbers (p95 targets, 22% session affinity, 120/300 token chat mix) midline reserved recommendation is: 22 A100e-equivalents dedicated (mixed 80% dense GPU + 20% memory-optimized) for sustained traffic with 30% burst headroom configured as autoscale.
- Costing note (rough): reserve monthly commit = $67k/month; burst overage priced separately with 1-minute preemptive spin-up on a different capacity pool.
- Risks: KV cache warm ratio and longer 600-token generate-batch calls increase memory pressure; propose enabling KV-prefix caching and limiting maximum concurrent long-run generates to a separate pool.

Can one of you confirm we have enough telemetry (token-level histograms + request latencies per endpoint) to validate the model assumptions? If not, we should ask Lagoon for a 48-hour trace export.

I’ll prepare a two-option deck: (A) conservative reserved (22 GPUs) and (B) lean reserved (14 GPUs + larger autoscale) with cost/latency tradeoffs.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Pre-sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Marissa, Marcus —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the two-option approach. Quick replies to your asks:

- We can export token-level histograms and per-endpoint latencies for the sample windows — I’ll have our SRE drop a 48-hour trace into the Drive link by EOD Monday.
- We are comfortable starting with the conservative reserved option if you think that reduces risk for our launch window; procurement wants the final monthly commit and SLA language to evaluate.

Next step from our side: I'll confirm procurement contact details and sign a mutual action plan once we have the formal quote. For now, please include the expected cold-start fallback behavior and model-variant routing notes in the proposal so we can surface to our platform team.

Thanks —
Aisha
